messages:
support_jane: @channel ACME is seeing ~30% of embedding inserts rejected by the indexer after a large backfill. Customer report: 'some vectors created but many failed with dim mismatch'. Ticket 12345 attached. Can eng take a look?
eng_indexer_oliver: Can you paste the raw indexer error for a failing doc? need the exact "expected/got" line.
customer_acme_bob: Pasting sample from their logs (redacted):
```
ERROR indexer.ingest: reject doc_id=acme_34 expected_dim=768 got_dim=512 model=acme-default-embed
HTTP 400 {"error":"vector dimension mismatch: expected 768, got 512"}
```
support_jane: Thanks Bob. Backfill started last night around 02:10 UTC using their in-house job. They upgraded our python SDK to 2.1.4 before the run.
eng_ml_raj: 512 vs 768 usually means mixed model versions. Could be the SDK switched default from text-embed-512 -> text-embed-768 depending on request. Any chance the batch mixed model names? That would produce mixed dims in one bulk request.
customer_acme_bob: Our job batches 1000 docs per request. We pin model at call site but the job uses two parallel workers with slightly different config files — one worker may still be using older model name. Oops.
devex_lina: FYI SDK 2.1.4 added an "auto_model" fallback for legacy calls — if model param absent it chooses a default per workspace. If some of their workers omitted the model param it could have silently picked a different dimension. We saw a similar report in a beta chat last month.
eng_indexer_oliver: Indexer receives an array of vectors in a single bulk RPC. When dims mismatch we reject the whole batch to keep index consistency. Rejection log format: `reject batch_id=... reason=dim_mismatch expected=768 got=512 sample_doc=acme_34`
eng_sre_anna: Also, SRE noticed a spike of 401/403s during the backfill window — looks like their token rotated mid-run which caused some retries and duplicate smaller batches. Not sure if that increased the chance of mixing.
infra_oncall_mike: Immediate steps we recommend: 1) Pause the customer's backfill job (they've paused it already). 2) Add a short-lived indexer-side validation endpoint to show expected_dim for their index. 3) Provide a reproducible curl/python snippet so they can validate before resuming.
support_jane: Can we give them a quick snippet to detect mixed dims client-side before sending? If so, we can unblock them to resume safely.
eng_ml_raj: Sure — suggest a local pre-check that samples embeddings for several docs and asserts consistent length. Example python snippet:
```
from redwood import EmbeddingsClient
c = EmbeddingsClient(api_key="REDACTED")
vecs = [c.embed_text(d) for d in sample_docs]
dims = set(len(v) for v in vecs)
assert len(dims) == 1, f"mixed dims {dims}"
```
devex_lina: I'll add an SDK helper `validate_batch_dimensions(samples)` to the next patch so users can run it easily.
eng_indexer_oliver: Long-term: we should improve error messaging to include which item in the batch caused the mismatch and the model name (if present). Current logs only show sample_doc id.
eng_sre_anna: Also saw a small billing anomaly — the backfill created partial successful inserts and customers were charged for both successful tokens and for failed retries. Finance wants a note if we advise a rerun.
support_jane: ACME wants a mitigation plan and a backfill plan that minimizes additional cost. They asked whether we can internally remap 512 -> 768 for failed docs — is that possible?
eng_ml_raj: You cannot safely "pad" or expand a 512 vector to 768; semantics would be wrong. Must re-run embeddings with the correct model. Two options: 1) Recompute only failed doc set with pinned model 768. 2) Run entire backfill again but with single-model guarantee. Option 1 is cheaper.
infra_oncall_mike: For the indexer side, we'll add an endpoint that lists failed doc ids for their last ingest attempt so they can target reruns. I'll open an internal ticket and give ETA ~3 hours for a small tool.
deploy_bot: deploy started: indexer/validation-endpoint v1.2 -> canary
eng_indexer_oliver: After the endpoint is up: recommended steps for ACME: 1) run client-side validate_batch_dimensions on a sample. 2) use our endpoint to fetch failed_ids. 3) re-run embeddings for failed_ids with pinned model name. 4) send a small verification batch. We'll help monitor.
support_jane: Action items:
- @infra_oncall_mike add failed_ids endpoint (owner: mike)
- @devex_lina add SDK validate helper (owner: lina)
- @eng_ml_raj write short note on model names/dims for CS (owner: raj)
- @customer_acme_bob resume backfill only after validation (owner: bob)
customer_acme_bob: Appreciate it. We'll hold and wait for the failed_ids list, then re-run only the failures. Please keep an eye on billing if they decide to rerun — we'll coordinate.
eng_sre_anna: One more note: warn them about token rotation mid-run. Recommend using a long-lived key for the backfill or coordinating rotation window.
infra_oncall_mike: I'll post the failed_ids link here in ~2.5h and tag you all. Will also include a small script to fetch and re-ingest.
support_jane: Thanks everyone. I'll update the ticket and let ACME know the timeline. :thumbsup:
